text:
alex: Heads-up — saw a regression on the canary run after the batching heuristic change (batch_timer_ms -> 6 -> 3). Latency P95 for short chats jumped and nsys shows a burst of H2D memcpy stalls when KV cache hit rate increases.

alex: Quick summary from the trace: multiple small H2D transfers back-to-back, DMA engine queues are saturated, kernels waiting on page faults for pageable allocations. Prefetching previously masked this, but with the new scheduler we appear to serialize peer transfers. :thinking:

alex: Here is the problematic snippet from the nsys timeline (condensed):
```
H2D memcpy  |  8us  | contiguous small chunks (~2-8KB)
kernel A    | 20us  | waiting on copy completion (stall)
peer-copy   | 12us  | retry queue due to DMA watermark
KV-hit      |  1us  | quick lookup, then triggers H2D for embeddings slice
```

alex: Observed flags: `alloc_type=pageable`, `kernel_choice=optimized_v2` (changed last week), `batch_size=8->12`, `kv_cache_hit_rate=0.82 -> 0.95`.

jordan: Interesting — so higher kv cache hit rate means more small H2D hot-paths (embedding slices) instead of single big transfer. The new kernel_choice probably swapped to a different peer-copy path that doesn't coalesce small transfers. Can you attach the full nsys `.qdrep`? :eyes:

alex: Uploaded the trace to GCS (link in thread). Quick grep of the NVTX markers shows lots of back-to-back `memcpyHtoD` with < 32KB sizes. Also saw host pinned allocator falling back to pageable for some requests: `pinned_alloc_failures=3` during the spike.

maya: Is the allocator's fallback synchronous? If pinned allocation failed and we tried to fallback to pageable, that can cause kernel stalls on first touch page faults. We should look at our pinned pool watermark and the prefetch policy.

perf-bot: automated-trace-analysis: Found pattern "many small H2D memcpy calls (2-16KB) spaced <100us apart". Suggested rules matched: {coalesce_window_us:200, prefer_pinned: true}.

jordan: Two immediate hypotheses: 1) kernel selection `optimized_v2` changed the scheduling of peer copies so DMA queue depth drops (no coalescing), 2) batch growth increases number of small slices and the allocator can't keep up with pinned pages causing page faults.

alex: Reproducer steps I used: run canary model with `--batch_timer_ms=3 --target_batch=12` on a machine with mixed pinned pool usage (simulated by running concurrent alloc-heavy tests). Reproduces in ~10-20 runs.

alex: Minimal mitigation that helped locally: forcing pinned allocations for embedding buffers and enabling `coalesce_window_us=250` in the DMA scheduler. P95 dropped back to baseline.

maya: Good. For next steps:
- capture full nsys + `nvlink_profile` output for a failing run
- add counters to kernel selection path to log when `optimized_v2` picks peer-copy vs direct memcpy
- increase pinned pool watermark for the canary to see if drop disappears

jordan: Also let's add an inexpensive sampler: record `avg memcpy size`, `memcpy_count_per_request`, `pinned_alloc_failures` to the request trace. That will help correlate without full traces.

alex: Agreed. I'll file a perf issue with traces + reproducer and assign to eng-runtime. In the ticket I'll include the quick patch that sets `coalesce_window_us=250` as a temporary guard.

maya: If we confirm allocator fallback is the culprit, we should consider changing the prefetch order: prefetch embedding pages before doing small memcpy bursts. We might also tweak batching to prefer fewer larger slices for KV hit common case.

perf-bot: note: scheduled a follow-up test job in 2h (canary group) with pinned_pool+coalesce_window applied. I'll post results. :thumbsup:

jordan: Thanks — tagging infra for help with reproducer machines: @infra-team please allocate a host with no other noisy workloads so we can validate DMA queue behavior.

alex: Thanks everyone — summary will go into the issue. If perf-bot run shows improvement I'll roll the temporary coalesce change to canary.

maya: One more callout: double-check quantized-kernel path too (`quant_kv_worker`) — if it uses smaller slices that could trigger the same pattern.

alex: noted.
